_what: Frozen counts for the two truncation-disclosure guards (DSR-660).
_why_a_ratchet: A capped result presented as a complete one is the same defect class as a transport failure reported as a zero. Almost all of this is upstream code that re-syncs from mims-harvard:main, so it is contained rather than rewritten. Both counts may fall, never rise.
_how_to_lower_slices: Make the function say what it cut: return a total, a truncated flag, or what is available alongside the capped list. The reference is FAERS _truncation_note -- a full page is evidence of truncation, not of completeness.
_how_to_lower_tools: Declare a companion total or truncated field in the tool's return_schema. A tool that accepts a limit and returns a short list gives the agent no way to tell the cap from the data.
_vocabulary: Observed, not invented. Derived from the complying half of the corpus: total 226, available 76, truncat 26, overflow 2, has_more 1, incomplete 1 (across the 599 functions taking a first-N slice). 'remaining' reads like an obvious term and occurs zero times, so it is deliberately excluded.
_note: The ticket's figures were 833 slices with 421 undisclosed, and did not reproduce: 875 first-N slices across 599 functions, of which 313 disclose nothing.
